thread:
nina-sales: Quick help please 1 ACME POC rotated keys and now sees `401 invalid_key` when they include X-Redwood-Org and X-Redwood-Project. Without headers the same secret works.

andre-eng: Can you paste the sanitized curl and the key suffix?

nina-sales: curl they used:
```
curl -s -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED-1b2c3d4e\" \
  -H \"X-Redwood-Org: acme-inc\" \
  -H \"X-Redwood-Project: demo\" \
  -d '{\"prompt\":\"ping\"}'
```
Key suffix: `1b2c3d4e`.

maya-platform: Looking up the key: suffix `1b2c3d4e` = project-scoped key created under project `demo-v2` (not org-wide). That's why it fails when they pass project `demo`. Project slugs must match exactly and are case-sensitive.

own-se: Also note scoping: if a key is created with a preset that omits embeddings, calls to /v1/embeddings will return `403 insufficient_scope`. If they plan to use both generate and embeddings, create an org key with both scopes or a project key with matching project header.

nina-sales: Customer insists the old key "just worked" before rotation. Did anything change server-side?

andre-eng: We rolled a stricter authproxy check that enforces project/org binding when headers are present. Previously we tolerated user keys with headers in some cases; we removed that fallback. infra deploy: authproxy v4.0.2.

ops-bot: deploy authproxy v4.0.2 -> success

maya-platform: For immediate unblock: either a) recreate an org-scoped key in their Console and update their backend, or b) update the X-Redwood-Project header to `demo-v2` to match key binding (not ideal if they want stable project names).

own-se: I can generate a short-lived org key (24h) with both generate+embeddings and share it securely during the call so they can validate quickly.

nina-sales: Please do. I'm scheduling a 25-min screen share at 10:00 PST. Can you join?

own-se: I'll join. Also remind them to keep secrets server-side (K8s secret / Vault) and not embed keys in client JS.

andre-eng: Also warn about quotas: project-scoped keys count against project quotas; org keys against org quotas. If they do load testing after switching keys they may hit `429`.

nina-sales: Post-call update: we created org key sk-org-9fffabcd, they switched their k8s secret, validated both /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. All green. They asked for a short checklist for POC key best practices.

andre-eng: I'll draft a one-page checklist: prefer org keys for POCs, pick required scopes, store secrets server-side, update K8s secrets and redeploy, revoke old keys after validation, monitor Console for rate/usage.

nina-sales: Great 1 thanks everyone, closing this thread unless anything else shows up.
